_note: Advanced V2 concept questions for matrices.

questions.title: Coordinates
questions.prompt: In a matrix, what do row and column indexes identify together?
questions.explanation: A row index and a column index point to a single cell in the grid.

questions.title: Neighbor check
questions.prompt: Which neighbors usually count in a four-direction grid search?
questions.explanation: Four-direction movement changes either the row or the column, not both. Diagonal movement changes both coordinates and is a different rule.

questions.title: Bounds guard
questions.prompt: Why check row and column bounds before reading grid[row][col]?
choices: To avoid indexing outside the grid
questions.explanation: A neighbor step can point outside the grid. Check bounds before reading the cell so the code does not crash on an invalid row or column.

questions.title: Visited state
questions.prompt: Why mark visited cells during a grid traversal?
choices: To avoid revisiting the same cell forever
To change every value to zero
questions.explanation: Visited memory prevents cycles and duplicate work when paths can lead back to old cells.

questions.title: Row scan
questions.prompt: A scan checks row 1 of [[2,3],[4,5]]. Which values are in that row?
questions.explanation: Row indexes start at 0, so row 1 is the second row. In the shown grid, that row contains 4 and 5.

questions.title: Transpose
questions.prompt: What does transpose do to coordinates?
choices: It swaps row and column positions
It reverses only the first row
questions.explanation: A value at row r, column c moves to row c, column r in the transposed grid.

questions.title: Diagonal movement
questions.prompt: What coordinate change moves down-right one step?
questions.explanation: A down-right diagonal move adds 1 to the row and 1 to the column. That is why it visits cells where the row and column move together.

questions.title: Matrix mistake
questions.prompt: What is a common matrix bug?
choices: Using the number of rows as the number of columns
questions.explanation: Rectangular grids can have different row and column counts, so each dimension needs its own limit.
